text:
marta: Heads-up: after landing the epilogue fusion patch last night we're seeing a 12-18% regression on long-seq workloads when QKV packing is enabled. repro in CI microbench.

alex: Ugh. Is this across all FlashAttention variants or just our fused path?

marta: Appears specific to fused attention kernel (fused_attn_epilogue). FlashA-variant1 and paged-attn fallback unaffected.

priya: Any changes to memory layout / strides? last diff touched interleaving for q/k/v to support in-register epilogue ops.

marta: We changed qkv layout from [B, H, S, 3, D] -> packed contiguous [B, H, S, D*3] to avoid copies in epilogue. saved a memcpy earlier but perf dropped in matmul stage.

dan: Can you paste the perf output?

marta: Sure. snippet from perf harness:
```
Benchmark: seq=2048, batch=1, heads=32, d_head=64, qkv_packed=true
kernel_fused_attn_epilogue   42.3%  18.7ms
kernel_qkv_pack_unpack       6.1%   2.7ms
kernel_softmax               15.4%  6.8ms
kernel_kv_cache_write        4.2%   1.9ms
other(cuda_memcpy)           31.9%  14.1ms
total                       44.2ms
```

priya: Interesting — lots of memcpy time. maybe our packing made some kernels do non-coalesced loads, causing extra prolog copies?

alex: Could be alignment. If the epilogue expects 128B-aligned vectors but packing shifts start, loads go slow. Did we change dtype or alignment?

marta: We aligned to 16 bytes for portability. previously Q,K,V were separate tensors each 64-byte aligned. packing changed the stride math.

perf-bot: automated test results: regression 14.2% on model=gpt-8k, seq=2048, quant=false. link: https://perf.internal/runs/1773

dan: Quick experiment: try packing but keep each q/k/v sub-block aligned (pad between). If padding cost < memcpy cost maybe wins.

alex: Also test epilogue fusion toggle: bias+rope fused vs bias and rope separate. We saw earlier that rope fusion increases register pressure and can slow matmul.

priya: Yep. For reference, run matrix: {packed: [true,false]} x {epilogue_fuse: [bias_only, bias+rope, none]} x {align: [packed_align,packed_unaligned]} and compare. small script: 
```
./bench_attention --model=gpt2 --seq=2048 --packed-qkv $P --epilogue=$E --align=$A
```

marta: Running matrix now on a single V100 node. will post results.

marta: Quick interim results:
- packed=true, epilogue=bias+rope, align=unaligned -> 18% regression
- packed=true, epilogue=bias_only, align=unaligned -> 6% regression
- packed=true, epilogue=bias+rope, align=packed_align -> 3% reg (within noise)
- packed=false, epilogue=bias+rope -> baseline

alex: Sounds like alignment + rope fusion interaction. rope increases load offsets, combined with misalignment it kills coalescing.

dan: Two mitigation options: 1) keep packing but enforce padding to maintain sub-block alignment; 2) revert qkv packing and instead do a temporary in-register pack at epilogue time (costly but localized); 3) let kernel selector prefer non-packed fused kernel for long seq.

priya: I'm leaning to padding + kernel selector heuristic: packing is still beneficial for small seq where memcpy dominates. we need per-workload selection.

marta: Agreed. I'll prototype a heuristic: if seq > 1024 and head_dim % 64 == 0 then require packed_align or fallback to non-packed fused kernel.

alex: Also add a quick micro-optimizer to epilogue: reduce register usage by splitting rope into two passes to avoid hurting matmul throughput. cheap to try.

marta: Created draft PR with two changes: add pad for packed layout and add kernel selector flag --prefer-nonpacked-longseq. linking: https://git.internal/r/epilogue-packing-fix

perf-bot: nightly run queued: job 1773-epilogue-fix.

priya: Nice. Can we also add a unit perf test for KV cache scenario? packing interacts with paged KV write (we saw 4% in kv write). ensure cache writes still coalesced.

marta: Yeah adding perf unit that simulates incremental decode / cache write patterns.

dan: If fixes look good, let's backport to the 2.8.x release branch since customers hit long sequence models.

alex: Also add a regression test in our CI gating that runs one long-seq fused-attn benchmark to catch future regressions. cheap and will catch layout changes.

marta: Will do. thanks all :thumbsup:

priya: Thx — ping me once the padded layout numbers are in, I'll help analyze flamegraphs.

perf-bot: flamegraph uploaded -> https://perf.internal/flame/1773_epilogue_fix

marta: posted updated numbers in PR, packed+pad+rope back to baseline on A100. leaving open to watch memory overhead tradeoffs.

alex: Great. next steps: land pad + selector, add CI perf test, follow-up micro-optimizations for rope splitting.

marta: Filing a follow-up ticket for epilogue register-pressure analysis and KV cache coalesce verification. ticket: INF-2154

dan: Good thread. short-term mitigation merged to canary. we'll monitor.
